newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee static on lack of dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee static on lack of dollar demand.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee was seen trading in a narrow range on Friday due to a lack of demand for dollars in the market, dealers said.
At 0500 GMT, the rupee was at 58.42 to the greenback after opening at its previous closing level of 58.43, they said.
"There is not much of demand for dollars because there is a lack of imports," said an American Express Bank dealer.
The Central Bank pushed the greenback down by one local cent and fixed on buying and selling at 58.4174 and 59.5976.
Dealers said the lack of demand has prompted banks to hold on to the greenback, which has created a surplus of dollars in the market.
They said the market has witnessed substantial inward remittances of late with monies coming in for investment in the country's stock market.
"This and a lack of commercial demand has created dollar pluses in the market," a dealer for a local bank said.
"There should be a big bill for this market to move up," a Standard Chartered Bank dealer said.
Overnight call money, which opened at 10 percent was at 9.5 percent with the market highly liquid.
